builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Transporting Quantiles to Codebook: Scalable Vector Quantization without Codebook Collapse
summary: FlowVQ replaces the standard VQ-VAE quantizer with jointly learned EMA/codebook-update schemes by transporting fixed even-quantile prior codes through a lightweight flow-matching probability flow ODE to define the codebook. It adds training-time complexity and extra compute for learning and integrating the flow, plus sensitivity to flow-training stability, while inference tokenization cost depends on the final implementation and may remain near standard VQ lookup if the codebook is materialized. It can fail through distribution mismatch between latent encodings and the transported prior, degraded reconstruction on high-precision data, or implementation overhead that negates the claimed utilization benefit.
rationale: It is relevant to constrained production only if the reader trains or fine-tunes tokenizer models, so the benefit must be validated on their workload rather than adopted as a drop-in serving improvement.
technique: Flow-based vector quantization via quantile transport

It adds training-time complexity and extra compute for learning and integrating the flow, plus sensitivity to flow-training stability, while inference tokenization cost depends on the final implementation and may remain near standard VQ lookup if the codebook is materialized. It can fail through distribution mismatch between latent encodings and the transported prior, degraded reconstruction on high-precision data, or implementation overhead that negates the claimed utilization benefit.
Abstract claims full codebook utilization, scalability, and improved codebook expressivity on image tokenization, generation, and high-precision tokenization tasks, without quantified factors.
